top_strengths.reason: The founder has real Auburn access, student-community visibility, research strengths, and local relevance that broad enterprise competitors do not.
Student housing operators face a more price-sensitive market in 2026 and public industry commentary highlights a gap between survey answers and actual renter behavior.
The market already pays for student housing intelligence through subscription platforms, and the service can start with paid pilots before expanding into retainers.

top_weaknesses.reason: Operators may only value this during leasing season or until they absorb the core insights, which makes recurring retention uncertain.
Enterprise intelligence vendors already exist, so this idea must stay narrow and action-oriented rather than trying to compete on raw data breadth.
There is no scalable viral or paid engine at launch; first customers depend on direct outreach and proof of value.

riskiest_assumption_test.assumption: Auburn-area student housing operators will pay a student founder for a local intelligence brief instead of relying on existing leasing reports, surveys, and internal intuition.

experiment.description: Build a list of 15 Auburn-area operators or leasing teams. Create one 3-page sample brief using public listings, pricing, amenities, reviews, and student interviews. Send highly tailored outreach offering a $250 pilot brief and ask for a short call.
experiment.pass_threshold: At least 3 meetings booked and 1 paid pilot closed from 15 targeted prospects within 14 days.

all_assumptions_ranked.assumption: Auburn-area student housing operators will pay a student founder for a local intelligence brief instead of relying on existing leasing reports, surveys, and internal intuition.
The insight can be made concrete enough to influence pricing or messaging decisions, not just be read and ignored.
Auburn campus access creates a real moat rather than a nice-sounding story.
A monthly retainer is sustainable beyond the first pilot.
